comparison: Both evaluations support the development and key properties of CAIS (C9, C10, C56, C69, C113, C130). OpenEval emphasizes the methodological clarity and mathematical formulation, while peer reviewers explicitly praise CAIS as a useful metric and appreciate the correction for amino acid usage variation. Strong agreement on this methodological innovation.

Perfect agreement on claims C75-C77, C118. Both evaluations support that CAIS and ENC successfully address GC content confounding that affects CAI. OpenEval focuses on the empirical demonstration in Figure 3 with appropriate statistical methods, while peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge.

Strong agreement on the core ISD finding (C11, C72, C87, C89-C91, C110, C136). Both evaluations accept the empirical result showing relationships between CAIS and intrinsically disordered protein domains. OpenEval notes the finding is unexpected but statistically robust; peer reviewers acknowledge this as a new discovery enabled by CAIS without challenging the result.

Agreement on claims C93, C143 regarding CAIS's advantage in controlling for amino acid composition. Both evaluations recognize this as a valid methodological strength. OpenEval notes this makes CAIS more reliable despite ENC showing stronger statistical power; peer reviewers explicitly appreciate this correction as addressing known issues with CAI comparisons.

Complete agreement on claims C94, C97-C100, C129. Both evaluations support the empirical finding about ISD relationships. OpenEval notes the theoretical explanations remain speculative hypotheses; peer reviewers accept the finding without raising concerns about the interpretation.

Full agreement on claims C103-C104. Both evaluations support this negative control result ruling out GC-biased gene conversion as a confounding factor. OpenEval emphasizes this validates CAIS as measuring selection rather than gene conversion; peer reviewers implicitly accept this interpretation without challenge.

Agreement on claims C107, C111 regarding domain age analysis. Both evaluations support the finding that selection strength is equal across domain ages. OpenEval notes this strengthens the main finding by ruling out recency bias; peer reviewers accept this without raising concerns.

Agreement on statistical methodology (C83, C85-C86, C153). Both evaluations support the appropriateness of the linear mixed model and phylogenetic correction approaches. OpenEval provides detailed justification for controlling for Pfam identity; peer reviewers implicitly accept these methods as appropriate.

Significant disagreement on claims C6, C38, C141 regarding CAIS as a more direct proxy for selection efficiency. OpenEval rates these claims as SUPPORTED with minor subjectivity noted; peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN with substantial skepticism, providing mathematical analysis showing mutation bias changes could impact CAIS independent of selection strength changes. This represents a fundamental theoretical disagreement.

Partial overlap on practical advantages (C142, C70). Both evaluations support the practical utility of codon-based metrics not requiring polymorphism data. OpenEval emphasizes the directness claim (which peer reviewers challenge elsewhere); peer reviewers focus on general applicability to any annotated genome.

OpenEval evaluates claims C40-C44 about CAI limitations for cross-species comparisons as SUPPORTED, noting the mathematical explanation and empirical demonstration. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these limitations motivate CAIS development which peer reviewers accept.

OpenEval evaluates claims C64-C68 about amino acid composition confounding as SUPPORTED with multiple literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers explicitly appreciate CAIS's correction for this issue (noted in R4).

OpenEval evaluates claims C149-C150, C133-C135 about dataset restrictions and rationales as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these methodological details are not explicitly discussed by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on phylogenetic correction methodology. OpenEval evaluates claims C151-C153 about phylogenetic independent contrasts as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers implicitly accept phylogenetic correction (C153) as part of the overall statistical approach without detailed discussion.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1-C5, C21-C25 establishing theoretical background from population genetics as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this foundational material.

OpenEval evaluates claims C28-C35 about limitations of Ne-based approaches as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these limitations motivate the study but are not explicitly discussed by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates claims C137-C140 about reconciling contradictory findings as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not explicitly address this reconciliation attempt.

OpenEval evaluates claims C120-C121 as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the limitation that the study cannot distinguish selection on codon bias versus GC content. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this relates to peer reviewers' broader theoretical concerns about CAIS interpretation.
